text:
Jordan: Hey team — first day yay! I'm following the local dev guide but can't get Postgres + Redis up with docker-compose on my M1 Mac. compose returns Postgres crashloop with 'database files are incompatible' and Redis exits with bind errors. Any quick pointers?
Maya: welcome Jordan :wave: most common is host Postgres already running (port conflict) or image arch mismatch on Apple Silicon. what does `docker ps -a` show?
Jordan: thanks! `docker ps -a` shows a postgres container restarting, image postgres:15, and a redis:latest exited (1). my local Postgres (homebrew) is running on 5432 actually.
Sam: if you have homebrew postgres running that will block 5432 — either stop it (`brew services stop postgresql`) or change the compose port mapping to something else like `5433:5432`.
Maya: also for M1/ARM, some official images are linux/amd64 by default and need platform override. In compose you can add `platform: linux/amd64` under the service or use an arm-friendly tag like `postgres:15-alpine` (but watch for compatibility).
Jordan: oh hmm I tried `platform: linux/amd64` and docker pulled an amd64 image but it failed with "exec format error".
Kevin: on Mac with M1 it's usually the opposite — amd64 images run under emulation (qemu) and work but are slower. "exec format error" sounds like an image for a different OS/arch. Which exact error? can you paste the container logs?
Jordan: logs:```postgres 2024-XX-XX 00:00:00.000 UTC [1] LOG: starting PostgreSQL 15... FATAL: database files are incompatible with server"``` Redis log:```1:C 01 Mar 00:00:00.000 # Fatal error, can't open config file '/usr/local/etc/redis/redis.conf'```
Maya: that Postgres msg usually means an existing data volume was created by a different Postgres version or arch. If you don't need the data, remove the volume: `docker-compose down -v` then `docker-compose up`. If you do need it, you'll need to run the same version that created it.
Jordan: ah that explains it — I had a leftover volume from a previous try. running `docker-compose down -v` now.
Devex Bot: Quick link: local dev setup guide https://redwood.example.internal/devex/run-local.md — section "Databases (Postgres/Redis)" has compose snippets and known M1 notes.
Sam: for Redis, check your compose mounts. If you're binding a host config path, make sure the file exists. Compose examples we use:
```yaml
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:15
    ports:
      - "5433:5432" # map to nonconflicting host port if needed
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: password
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U postgres"]
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
    command: ["redis-server", "--save", "60", "1"]
volumes:
  pgdata:
```
Kevin: if you run into permission errors on the pgdata volume on mac, try `chown -R 1000:1000 ./data` where `1000` is the container uid, or use a named Docker volume instead of a host bind to avoid macOS filesystem permission issues.
Jordan: `docker-compose down -v` removed the volume, `docker-compose up` pulled redis:7-alpine and postgres:15 and both came up! :tada: I had to stop my homebrew postgres too.
Maya: nice. two extra tips: 1) if you want faster startup on M1, prefer the alpine/arm images when available; 2) add a small healthcheck wait in your app startup to avoid race conditions.
Jordan: hugely helpful — thanks everyone. One last q: should I change my compose to host ports 5433/6379 (if I'm also running local Redis)?
Sam: change only if you actually run local services. For Redis it's common to leave docker-mapped 6379:6379 unless host has it. For Postgres, pick 5433 or stop host service. We include env override file `.env.local` in the repo where you can set `PGHOST=localhost\nPGPORT=5433` to avoid hardcoding.
Jordan: I'll add `.env.local` and update my prefs. Thanks again :pray:
